title: multi-gpu-parallelism-nccl-scaling-experiments-wip
content:
Summary:

This is a working doc for the multi-GPU parallelism performance investigation focused on NCCL/interconnect limits and how they affect tensor- and pipeline-parallel configurations in our serving runtime. Primary goal: identify dominant bottlenecks for common serving workloads (decoder-only LLMs, seq_len 2048, batch sizes 1-16) and produce mitigations we can apply at runtime (grouping strategies, topo-aware placement, NCCL env config).

High-level findings (preview):
- Within-node NVLink/NVSwitch gives excellent bandwidth for tensor-parallel AllReduce/AllGather; for up to 8 GPUs on a node we see near-linear scaling for matmul-heavy workloads.
- Cross-node communication (HDR100/HDR200/InfiniBand, AWS EFA) is the main limiter for pipeline-parallel workloads once model partitions span machines: AllGather/ReduceScatter latency and tail behaviors dominate end-to-end tail latency.
- NCCL algorithm selection and topology awareness matter: RING scales well for large message sizes but suffers for many ranks with small message sizes (typical of KV cache scatter/gather patterns); TREE/CollNet variants improve latency for small messages but reduce peak throughput in some cases.
- Hierarchical grouping (intra-node tensor-parallel first, inter-node pipeline groups) reduces cross-node bandwidth pressure and improves tail latency.

Goals / Questions:
- Quantify where cross-node links saturate for our target models (token throughput vs tail latency curves).
- Determine which NCCL configs (ALGO, P2P, COLLNET flags, LL/LL128) give best tradeoffs for serving workloads vs training-like throughput tests.
- Validate runtime strategies: group size heuristics, topo-aware placement, dynamic fallback to single-node TensorParallel (with model swap) when interconnect limited.

Hardware & software testbeds:
- On-prem cluster (lab): DGX A100 (8xA100 40GB, NVSwitch intra-node), Mellanox HDR200 between nodes, OS: Ubuntu 20.04, CUDA 11.7, NCCL 2.14, OFED stack.
- AWS baseline: p4d.24xlarge (8xA100) with EFA, libfabric + NCCL; also c7gn for networking checks.
- Mini-cluster: 4x single-GPU G5 instances connected over standard EC2 fabric to test low-bandwidth cases.
- Tools: nccl-tests (allreduce/allgather/alltoall), NVIDIA Nsight Systems (nsys), nvprof traces where needed, torch.profiler + NVTX, tcpdump + perf for host-level events, bpftrace for kernel-level scheduling anomalies.

Workloads / Benchmarks:
- Synthetic nccl-tests for microbenchmarks: messages sizes 1KB -> 8MB, ranks 2 -> 64.
- Model-level (serving harness): GPT-like 7B and 33B decoder-only models instrumented to report per-stage latencies (forward, allgather, kv-restore), KV cache behavior for generation (prefix reuse). Sequence lengths: 512/1024/2048. Batches: 1, 4, 8, 16.
- Real request traces (anonymized): single token generation vs multi-token bursts to observe tail effects.

Experiment matrix (examples):
- Vary group sizes: (tensor groups within node) x (pipeline partitions across nodes). Example: 8-GPU node -> tensor group sizes 2,4,8; pipeline partitions 1->2->4 nodes.
- NCCL env variations: NCCL_ALGO=RING/TREE, NCCL_IB_HCA=/dev/mlx5_0, NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0/1, NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD values.
- Message patterns: small (KV gather 512B-4KB) vs large (activations 256KB-4MB).

Representative results (selected):
- nccl-tests allgather (8 GPUs within node): bandwidth ~ 700 GB/s aggregate (matches NVSwitch spec). Cross-node (2 nodes, 8+8 GPUs): allgather bandwidth drops to ~40-80 GB/s depending on HDR link saturation and algorithm.
- Model run (7B, seq=2048, batch=1) with 2-node pipeline: median token latency ~120 ms, 95th ~320 ms. Same config but grouping tensor parallel inside nodes reduces 95th to ~180 ms.
- For small message sizes (<8KB) ring algorithm introduced 95th tail spikes up to 2x of median for rank counts >= 16. Switching to NCCL_ALGO=TREE and enabling COLLNET (where supported) reduced small-message tail variance by ~30% at the cost of ~5-10% aggregate throughput for large messages.

Profiling notes / flame insights:
- NVTX ranges show time spent in AllGather is often dominated by wait for slowest rank (network jitter / NIC scheduling).
- Host CPU overhead for posting RDMA ops becomes visible in torch.profiler for many small-message patterns; pins to a single CPU core can exacerbate queuing delays.
- On AWS, we observed higher jitter for cross-AZ tests; EFA libfabric config (TX size, provider selection) matters.

Root causes / interpretation:
- Tail latency is a mix of network link saturation and scheduling-induced jitter (host NIC driver, kernel interrupts, CPU core contention).
- Algorithm mismatch: ring is throughput-optimal for big contiguous messages; serving often has many small/medium messages (KV cache shards, attention KV gathers) so algorithm choice matters.
- Topology mismatch: naive one-rank-per-GPU across nodes treats all links equal; hierarchical/nested allreduce that prefer intra-node NVLink avoids hitting the slower inter-node fabric.

Mitigations to test/implement in runtime (shortlist):
1) Default to hierarchical groups: prefer full tensor-parallel groups inside a node; only do global collectives for pipeline syncs. Implement group math in planner and make it adjustable by SLO profile.
2) NCCL env presets per workload: small-message preset -> NCCL_ALGO=TREE, LL_RAIL (if supported), COLLNET on supported topologies. Large-message preset -> RING for throughput.
3) Adaptive fallback: if a pipeline stage reports rising allgather tail latency beyond threshold, shrink pipeline across fewer nodes and increase local tensor-parallel (with model-reload handshake).
4) Kernel/CPU tuning: pin NIC IRQ affinities, use isolcpus for the serving process where possible to reduce host-side jitter. Document recommended host kernel and NIC driver versions.
5) Batching hints: expose KV-cache-aware batching to avoid many small cross-node messages during generation; coalesce KV updates from multiple requests when possible within latency SLOs.

Open experiments / TODOs:
- Quantify benefit/cost of COLLNET across all our lab topologies (some NICs/drivers show regressions). ENG-1723.
- End-to-end test of adaptive fallback (pipeline shrink + model swap) under realistic traffic via chaos tests.
- Investigate using NCCL_P2P_DISABLE for certain topologies to force hierarchical algorithms and measure impact.
- Run long-duration jitter tests (>24h) on AWS p4d to catch rare tail events.

Appendix: quick run commands and notes
- nccl-tests example: ./build/all_gather_perf -b 1 -e 8388608 -f 2 -g <num_gpus>
- env examples: export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; export NCCL_ALGO=RING; export NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=2097152; export NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=1
- tracing: nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=trace ./serve_benchmark --model 7B --seq 2048

Contacts / owners: Ava Chen (owner of experiment), Miguel Torres (network profiling lead), Priya Nair (serving runtime integration).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; please add missing test cases you care about and link any customer incidents where cross-node generation tails were observed.
- If you have specific infra to test (e.g., HPE Slingshot, custom Mellanox firmware), add it to infra inventory and we'll queue runs.

Change log (brief):
- 2025-01-15 created initial matrix and baseline nccl-tests.
- 2025-01-28 added AWS p4d runs and NVTX traces.
- 2025-02-20 added preliminary mitigation list and updated small-message results.

Unresolved questions:
- Is it acceptable to bias default planner towards intra-node TP even if it increases cold-start model load time? (tradeoff: lower steady-state tail vs slightly higher startup latency).
- How to expose NCCL presets to customers using Private deployments without exposing low-level env variables? (config abstractions needed).

End.
